title: DSPE: An Energy-Efficient Edge Processor for Deepseek Inference with Merkletree-Based Incremental Pruning, Multi-Stage Boothing Lookup and Dynamic Adaptive Posit Processing
evidence_span: DSPE targets energy-constrained DeepSeek edge inference with MerkleTree-based incremental pruning, bit-flip-aware approximate multiplication through multi-stage lookup, and a dynamic adaptive posit format with hardware multiplication; the official description reports TSMC 28nm implementation and 91.7 TFLOPS/W against state-of-the-art designs.

title: MATCHA: Efficient Deployment of Deep Neural Networks on Multi-Accelerator Heterogeneous Edge SoCs
evidence_span: MATCHA generates concurrent schedules for heterogeneous accelerators, uses constraint programming for L3/L2 allocation and scheduling, and applies pattern matching, tiling, and mapping across hardware units; on MLPerf Tiny with two heterogeneous accelerators it reports up to 35% lower inference latency relative to the MATCH compiler and improved utilization.
problem: Existing DNN deployment frameworks do not exploit heterogeneous accelerator engines effectively on edge SoCs.
method_or_artifact: Unified deployment framework combining constraint-programmed memory/schedule optimization with pattern matching, tiling, and per-unit mapping.
workload_or_benchmark: MLPerf Tiny on an SoC containing two heterogeneous accelerators; model suite, SoC details, and latency measurement conditions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-accelerator heterogeneous edge SoC with L3/L2 memory hierarchy; accelerator types, memory capacities, clocking, and compiler versions are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 35% inference-latency reduction relative to MATCH
limits: The description does not give model-by-model latency, utilization, energy, memory traffic, or schedule overhead.

title: TRAC: Transparent Row Activation Counting for Efficient Rowhammer Monitoring
evidence_span: TRAC monitors DRAM row activations with ACT-triggered updates, in-subarray processing, and an LFSR-based counter, aiming to avoid the timing overhead of PRAC; circuit and system evaluations report correctness, stability, negligible area cost, and no timing overhead, without numeric values.
problem: Per-row activation counting defenses against RowHammer can lengthen critical DRAM timing parameters and reduce performance.
method_or_artifact: Transparent row activation counting architecture with ACT-triggered update, in-subarray processing, and LFSR-based counting.
workload_or_benchmark: RowHammer monitoring in DRAM with circuit-level simulation and system-level evaluation; attack patterns, DRAM organization, and timing suite are unspecified.

limits: No numeric area, energy, latency, security coverage, false-positive, or disturbance thresholds are supplied.

title: Active Imitation Learning for Thermal- and Kernel-Aware LFM Inference on 3D S-NUCA Many-Cores
evidence_span: AILFM learns thermal-aware thread-migration and V/f policies from Oracle demonstrations for 3D S-NUCA many-cores, modeling core variation and kernel behavior while maintaining thermal safety across diverse large-foundation-model workloads; the official description reports improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines without numeric values.
problem: 3D S-NUCA systems offer bandwidth and locality but introduce thermal constraints and non-uniform cache latency, making migration and voltage/frequency control difficult for diverse LFM kernels.
method_or_artifact: Active imitation-learning scheduler trained from Oracle thermal policies with kernel-aware and core-aware policy features.

title: MASQ: Accelerating Masked Diffusion via Stage-Wise Multi-Precision Quantization
evidence_span: MASQ co-designs masked-diffusion precision and hardware: stage-wise MXINT8/4/2 assignment follows spatial and semantic importance, timestep-aware scheduling reduces redundant work, and a block-wise multi-precision engine and mask-management unit implement the design; the official description reports up to 16.06x/5.39x speedup and 4.18x/4.93x energy-efficiency gains over A100/Orin NX while preserving quality.
problem: Masked diffusion repeatedly processes unmasked regions, creating computational redundancy and high energy cost.
method_or_artifact: Stage-wise mixed-precision assignment, timestep-aware scheduling, block-wise multi-precision compute, and mask management hardware.
workload_or_benchmark: Masked diffusion image generation; quality metric, image sizes, model, mask distributions, and sampling steps are unspecified.
